target.title: fix(codex): preserve UTF-16 pairs in tool output delta truncation
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `CodexAppServerEventProjector` tool output delta streaming produces a lone high surrogate when a non-BMP character (emoji) straddles the `remainingChars` truncation boundary. The `.slice(0, remainingChars)` call on line 1447 cuts at a UTF-16 code unit boundary, and when the cut point lands on a HIGH surrogate whose paired LOW surrogate falls just beyond the limit, the truncated chunk ends with a dangling `\uD83D`-style byte that corrupts tool output display.

## Why This Change Was Made

`truncateUtf16Safe` is already imported on line 29 and used elsewhere in the same file (lines 3413, 3435) — this single call site was missed. The fix replaces `.slice(0, remainingChars)` with `truncateUtf16Safe(delta, remainingChars)`, using the same canonical helper.

## User Impact

Streaming tool output from Codex app-server sessions no longer risks rendering corrupted surrogate bytes when model-generated tool output contains emoji characters near the output size limit boundary. No user-visible impact for ASCII-only tool output.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** The 8,000-char `TOOL_PROGRESS_OUTPUT_MAX_CHARS` progress-message cap can split a non-BMP character's surrogate pair when `remainingChars` lands on the HIGH surrogate. The fix uses `truncateUtf16Safe` to back off before the surrogate pair.

**Real environment tested:** Node.js v22.22.0, x64, linux

### 1. Production module proof (truncateUtf16Safe from packages/normalization-core)

The proof script imports the real production `truncateUtf16Safe` — no reimplementation:

```
node --import tsx proof-codex-event-projector-utf16.mjs
```

**Evidence after fix:**
```
=== POSITIVE (fix: truncateUtf16Safe from production module) ===

module: packages/normalization-core/src/utf16-slice.js
[c1] remaining=1, delta=😀hello (surrogate split)  chars=7999/8000 deltaCount=2
  ok: no lone surrogates
[c2] remaining=2, delta=😀 (exactly fits)  chars=8000/8000
  ok: emoji intact
  ok: no lone surrogates
[c3] remaining=2, delta=x😀y (cut at HIGH surrogate)  chars=7999/8000
  ok: no lone surrogates
  ok: emoji excluded cleanly
[c4] ASCII: remaining=10, delta=10 chars  chars=8000/8000
  ok: chunks clean
```

**Negative control (pre-fix behavior reproduced in the same script):**
```
=== NEGATIVE (old: .slice(0, remainingChars)) ===

[n1] remaining=1, delta=😀hello  chars=8000/8000
  BUG: lone surrogate U+D83D at [0] "\ud83d"
  ok: bug reproduced (lone surrogate emitted)
[n2] remaining=2, delta=x😀y (cut after HIGH, before LOW)  chars=8000/8000
  BUG: lone surrogate U+D83D at [1] "x\ud83d"
  ok: bug reproduced (lone surrogate emitted)

=== Summary ===
node=v22.22.0 MAX=8000 source=production truncateUtf16Safe
ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS: 8 passed, 0 failed
```

### 2. Real CodexAppServerEventProjector regression test (vitest)

A focused regression test drives the real `CodexAppServerEventProjector` through `handleNotification` → `handleOutputDelta` → `emitToolResultMessage` with `verboseLevel: "full"` and `onToolResult` spy. Three scenarios cross the 8,000-char progress cap:

- **Case 1:** `remainingChars=1`, delta starts with 😀 → old code cuts lone HIGH surrogate
- **Case 2:** `remainingChars=2`, delta=`x😀y` → old code cuts after HIGH, before LOW
- **Case 3:** ASCII-only boundary → no regression

**Positive (fix applied):**
```
pnpm test extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.test.ts \
  -t "keeps streamed progress output UTF-16 safe"

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed | 146 skipped (147)
```

**Negative control (fix reverted to main's `.slice(0, remainingChars)`):**
```
 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  1 failed | 146 skipped (147)
 ❯ extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.test.ts:3797:24
    3795|     expect(allTexts.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    3796|     for (const text of allTexts) {
    3797|       expect(text).not.toMatch(LONE_SURROGATE);
       |                        ^
    3798|     }
    3799|   });
```

The real projector's `onToolResult` callback received text containing a lone surrogate — the test catches the exact bug this PR fixes.

**Negative control restored to fix — passes again:**
```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed | 146 skipped (147)
```

**Existing adjacent tests also pass (no regression):**
```
pnpm test extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.test.ts \
  -t "keeps final command|keeps streamed command|keeps streamed progress|freezes streamed raw prefix"

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  4 passed | 143 skipped (147)
```

## Evidence

- **Vitest regression test:** `extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.test.ts` — new test "keeps streamed progress output UTF-16 safe at the 8,000-char progress message cap" drives real `CodexAppServerEventProjector` through the progress truncation boundary with 3 UTF-16 edge cases
- **Production module proof:** `proof-codex-event-projector-utf16.mjs` imports real `truncateUtf16Safe` from `packages/normalization-core/src/utf16-slice.js` — 6 positive + 2 negative control assertions, all passing
- **Negative control:** Both proof script and vitest test verified: reverting fix → lone surrogate emitted → test fails
- **Change surface:** 1 file, 1 line — `delta.slice(0, remainingChars)` → `truncateUtf16Safe(delta, remainingChars)`
- **Canonical helper:** `truncateUtf16Safe` already imported (line 29) and used at 2 other call sites in the same file
